source_text: Neque enim in sacrificiis quae Abel et Cain primi optulerunt munera eorum Deus, sed corda intuebatur, ut ille placeret in munere qui placebat in corde. Abel pacificus et iustus, dum Deo sacrificat innocenter, docuit et ceteros, quando ad altare munus offerunt, sic uenire cum Dei timore, cum simplici corda, cum lege iustitiae, cum concordiae pace. merito ille dum in sacrificio Dei talis est, ipse postmodum sacrificium Deo factus est, ut martyrium primus ostendens initiaret sanguinis sui gloria dominicam passionem qui et iustitiam Domini habuerat et pacem. tales denique a Domino coronantur, tales in die iudicii cum Domino uindicabuntur. ceterum discordans et dissidens et pacem cum fratribus non habens, secundum quod beatus apostolus et scriptura sancta testatur, nec si pro nomine occisus fuerit, crimen dissensionis fraternae poterit euadere, quia sicut scriptum est qui fratrem suum odit homicida est, nec ad regnum [caelorum] peruenit aut cum Deo uiuit homicida. non potest esse cum Christo qui imitator Iudae maluit esse quam Christi. quale delictum est quod nec baptismo sanguinis potest ablui, quale crimen est quod martyrio non potest expiari!
thought_title: The sacrifice of the discordant cannot be cleansed even by martyrdom
orientation: Cyprian is explaining why peace and concord are the true sacrifice God accepts, using Abel and Cain as the first examples.
pass_a_gloss: For indeed in the sacrifices which Abel and Cain first offered God did not look at their gifts but at their hearts, so that he who was pleasing in heart might be pleasing in gift. Abel, peaceable and just, while he sacrifices to God innocently, taught also the rest, when they offer a gift at the altar, to come thus with the fear of God, with a simple heart, with the law of justice, with the peace of concord. Deservedly he, while he is such in the sacrifice of God, was himself afterwards made a sacrifice to God, so that, first showing martyrdom, he inaugurated the Lord's passion with the glory of his blood, he who had both the justice of the Lord and peace. Such men are finally crowned by the Lord, such men will be vindicated with the Lord on the day of judgment. But the discordant and dissenting man and the one not having peace with brothers, according to what the blessed apostle and holy scripture testifies, not even if he will have been killed for the name will he be able to escape the crime of fraternal dissension, because as it is written he who hates his brother is a murderer, and a murderer does not reach the kingdom of heaven or live with God. He cannot be with Christ who preferred to be an imitator of Judas rather than of Christ. What a fault it is that cannot be washed away even by the baptism of blood, what a crime it is that cannot be expiated by martyrdom!

choices.why: The singular 'corda' is a variant or error for 'corde'; the sense is clearly singular 'heart', matching the earlier contrast between heart and gift.
The verb 'initiaret' means to begin or initiate; Abel's martyrdom is presented as the first instance prefiguring Christ's passion.
The passive of 'uindico' here means to be avenged or vindicated, i.e., to receive justice in their favor on judgment day.

choices.term: nec si pro nomine occisus fuerit
choices.english: not even if he will have been killed for the name
choices.why: The phrase 'pro nomine' refers to being killed for the name of Christ; the future perfect 'occisus fuerit' is kept as a future perfect in the gloss to preserve the conditional force.
rejected: even if he is killed for the name

choices.why: This is the technical term for martyrdom as a baptism; the literal rendering preserves the theological weight.

bible_refs.note: qui fratrem suum odit homicida est

pass_b_english: For in the sacrifices that Abel and Cain first offered, God was not looking at their gifts but at their hearts, so that the one who was pleasing in heart was pleasing in his gift. Abel, peaceful and just, while sacrificing to God innocently, taught the rest of us that when we bring an offering to the altar, we should come with the fear of God, with a simple heart, with the law of justice, with the peace of concord. Rightly, since he was such a man in his sacrifice to God, he himself afterward became a sacrifice to God, so that by being the first to show martyrdom he inaugurated the Lord's passion with the glory of his own blood—he who had both the justice and the peace of the Lord. Such people are crowned by the Lord, and such people will be vindicated with the Lord on the day of judgment. But the one who is quarrelsome and divisive and does not have peace with his brothers, as the blessed apostle and holy Scripture testify, will not be able to escape the crime of fraternal dissension even if he will have been killed for the name, because as it is written, whoever hates his brother is a murderer (1 John 3:15), and a murderer does not reach the kingdom of heaven or live with God. The one who preferred to be an imitator of Judas rather than of Christ cannot be with Christ. What a sin it is that cannot be washed away even by the baptism of blood! What a crime it is that cannot be expiated even by martyrdom!
notes: The source has 'cum simplici corda' where 'corde' is expected; this is likely a textual variant or scribal error. The gloss renders the intended singular sense.

last_rejected.quote: whoever hates his brother is a murderer (1 John 3:15)
last_rejected.source_quote: qui fratrem suum odit homicida est
last_rejected.why: Source quotes 1 John 3:15 but source text lacks citation; English adds it without basis.
last_rejected.fix: whoever hates his brother is a murderer, and a murderer does not reach the kingdom of heaven or live with God.
last_rejected.ruling: Source 'sicut scriptum est' signals scripture; 1 John 3:15 is correct reference. Adding citation aids reader, not misleading.

last_rejected.quote: he inaugurated the Lord's passion with the glory of his own blood
last_rejected.source_quote: initiaret sanguinis sui gloria dominicam passionem
last_rejected.why: Latin 'initiaret' means 'initiated/began,' not 'inaugurated'; 'gloria' is ablative of means, 'by the glory.'
last_rejected.fix: he initiated the Lord's passion by the glory of his own blood
last_rejected.ruling: 'Inaugurated' is valid for 'initiaret'; 'with glory' correctly renders ablative 'gloria.' Mere preference, not error.

last_rejected.why: 'corda' is neuter plural (hearts), not singular; 'simple heart' misrepresents the Latin grammar.
last_rejected.ruling: 'corda' likely scribal error for 'corde'; 'simple heart' matches context 'cum Dei timore.' Not a real mistranslation.
